Information since September signals a demand-side soft patch centered in business fixed investment and exports, while the labor market remains firm; easing the funds rate to 1.50–1.75% and using T-bill purchases/repo operations to maintain ample reserves is consistent with rule-like stabilization (Taylor; McCallum and Nelson, 1999) and New Keynesian evidence that expectations drive inflation dynamics (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido), especially when market-based inflation compensation is low. Given investment’s outsized contribution to short-run GDP fluctuations, the cut should cushion activity (Sims, 1992; B. Friedman), though the two dissents underscore residual uncertainty; overall the tone is cautiously constructive.
